findings.title: Date-override path bypasses busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot falls inside a date override, dateOverrideExist is set to true and checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 135 without reaching the busy.every(...) check at line 153. Consequently calendar events and existing Cal bookings are ignored for every slot on an override day, so a fixed or round-robin host can be double-booked on days with a date override.

findings.title: Dayjs object identity comparison never detects empty overrides
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so it is always false. The branch intended to recognize a zero-length override (start equals end, i.e. unavailable for that override period/day) is dead code, and such overrides are not handled as intended.

findings.title: Slots only partially overlapping a date override are accepted
findings.body: The override test only rejects slots that end at/before the override start or start after the override end. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, starts inside it and ends after it, or starts exactly at override end (slotStartTime.isAfter(end) is false when equal) falls through to dateOverrideExist and is returned as available. checkIfIsAvailable therefore does not enforce that the whole [slotStart, slotEnd) interval is contained in the override, allowing fixed-host bookings partially outside their override availability.

findings.title: Working-hours guard uses slot start twice and lets non-working days pass
findings.body: In the workingHours.find callback, both start and end are computed from slotStartTime.hour()/minute(), so a slot starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime is accepted. Additionally, find only returns true when a working hour exists for slotStartTime.day() and the slot is outside it: if no working hour includes that weekday at all, or another same-day range covers the slot while an earlier range does not, the logic either falls through to the busy check as available or incorrectly rejects. This defeats the new fixed-host filtering for hosts whose hours end earlier, who don't work that day, or who have split ranges.

findings.title: No test covers round-robin fixed-host date overrides
findings.body: The only added test re-queries a single-user event (hosts: []) with a different invitee timezone. It does not create a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host and a loose host, does not give only the fixed host a date override, and does not exercise the new checkIfIsAvailable dateOverrides/workingHours filtering added for fixed/loose hosts in slots.ts. The main scenario described in the PR (slots must be limited by the fixed host's override) can regress without any test failing.
